definitions: A superstitious belief or story, typically one that is old and widely believed but has no basis in fact.
A piece of traditional advice or belief that is now considered to be unscientific or incorrect.
examples: My grandmother always said that eating carrots helps you see in the dark, but I think that's just an old wives' tale.
The idea that you'll catch a cold from going out with wet hair is a common old wives' tale.
Many people still believe the old wives' tale that feeding a cold and starving a fever is good advice.
